newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares pare gains in late electronic trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares pare gains in late electronic trade.

text.p: German shares pare gains in late electronic trade, with the main spur behind the losses coming from a weak opening on Wall Street and a softening of the dollar against the mark.
By 1352 GMT the IBIS DAX index was down 2.98 points, or 0.08 percent, at 3,749.39 points, while the June DAX future contract was unchanged at 3,749 points.
"Volumes are not huge today, and we reckon that the DAX will probably hang around the 3,700-point level by Friday," said a Munich trader.
The Dow Jones index was down about 10 points in early trade, which weighed on a German market that has slavishly been following the U.S. markets in recent weeks.
Some traders said the DAX would remain within a trading range from 3,700 to 3,750 points ahead of Friday's "triple witching" expiry of DAX futures, DAX options and stock options.
"The drop in late trade is normal profit-taking after such a strong advance," said one Frankfurt trader. "I do not expect much for this week and suspect we will see more steady trade."
The DAX ended bourse trade on Monday at a record closing high in a catch-up to Wall Street's gains on Friday.

The market generally ignored news from the European Union summit in Amsterdam where finance ministers clinched agreement on a pact that will link budget discipline among members of the bloc's planned single currency to economic growth and jobs.

The accord lifted one of the main obstacles to progress at a two-day summit of EU leaders, defusing what had threatened to be a serious rift between Bonn and Paris, the bloc's twin economic and political powerhouses.
Traders said the market's lack of reaction showed it had expected that a deal would be reached.
Export-sensitive shares remained in the spotlight in late dealings as chemical group Bayer AG led trading volumes and rose 10 pfennigs to 67.46 marks.
Rival chemical group Hoechst AG rose 65 pfennigs to 70.40 marks in IBIS dealings after a major U.S. investment house raised Hoechst to a market outperformer.

Hoechst also got a boost on market speculation that it would sell its Messer Griesheim industrial gas unit to Linde AG. Both companies denied the rumours. Linde shares rose 25 marks to 1,325 marks in late IBIS dealings.
